summary:
BEYOND SPACE is an interactive web application designed to make exploring and understanding NASA's SPHEREx space observations easier and more engaging. It transforms astronomical data into accessible visual experiences through three key features: Sky Explorer, Space Comparison, and Cosmic Time-Lapse.

Sky Explorer allows users to search for specific regions of the sky using celestial coordinates, detector selection, and observation dates. Space Comparison enables users to examine two observations of the same region side by side and visualize differences in brightness and detected features. Cosmic Time-Lapse combines multiple observations chronologically into a video, helping users observe potential changes over time without manually opening individual images.

By simplifying access to astronomical observations and providing intuitive visualization and comparison tools, BEYOND SPACE helps students, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers explore the universe more effectively. It bridges the gap between complex scientific datasets and interactive space exploration, making NASA's SPHEREx observations easier to understand and investigate.
details:
BEYOND SPACE is an interactive space exploration platform developed to make NASA's SPHEREx astronomical observations easier to access, explore, compare, and understand. The project uses data from NASA's Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx) mission, which observes the universe in infrared wavelengths ranging approximately from 0.75 to 5 micrometers.

Our application provides three major features:

1. Sky Explorer

Sky Explorer allows users to explore specific regions of the sky by entering celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), selecting a search region, choosing one of SPHEREx's six detectors (D1–D6), and specifying an observation date range. The application retrieves matching astronomical observations and displays the available images and their associated metadata. This makes it easier to explore historical observations of selected regions without manually searching through complex astronomical archives.

2. Space Comparison

Space Comparison allows users to select two observations of the same sky region and examine them side by side. Through image comparison and difference visualization, users can identify potential variations in brightness, visible features, and source positions. A difference heatmap helps highlight pixels that have changed between observations, making the comparison more intuitive and visually informative.

3. Cosmic Time-Lapse

Cosmic Time-Lapse transforms multiple observations of the same sky region into a chronological video. Users select the region, detector, and available observations. The application arranges the selected images according to their observation dates and combines them into a time-lapse video. This allows users to visualize observations over time instead of manually opening and switching between individual images.

Benefits and Intended Impact

BEYOND SPACE makes astronomical data more approachable through an interactive and visual experience. It can benefit students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers by simplifying access to historical observations, supporting visual comparisons, and helping users identify potential changes in astronomical sources. Our goal is to encourage curiosity about the universe, promote scientific exploration, and bridge the gap between complex astronomical datasets and everyday users.

Technologies and Tools Used

Our project combines web development technologies and astronomical data-access tools.

  • NASA SPHEREx Mission Data: Provides infrared astronomical observations.
  • NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA): Used to access SPHEREx observation data.
  • IRSA Simple Image Access (SIA) API: Used to search for observations matching selected sky coordinates and other query parameters.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript: Used for the web application's interface and interactive features.
  • Python: Used for backend processing and data handling, if included in the deployed implementation.
  • Image-processing techniques: Used to display, compare, and visualize astronomical observations.
  • Video-generation tools: Used to combine chronological observation images into a time-lapse video.

Creativity and Innovation

The creativity of BEYOND SPACE lies in bringing three connected capabilities—astronomical image exploration, observation comparison, and time-lapse generation—into a single platform. Instead of presenting users with raw scientific datasets, we transform observations into interactive visual experiences. The time-lapse feature provides a particularly engaging way to explore observations across different dates, while the comparison feature makes potential differences easier to notice.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several important factors:

  • Scientific accuracy: Ensuring that observations are associated with the correct sky region, detector, and observation dates.
  • Data accessibility: Making astronomical archive data easier to discover and explore.
  • User experience: Designing a simple interface that beginners can understand without advanced astronomy knowledge.
  • Visual clarity: Presenting astronomical images and differences in an understandable format.
  • Performance: Considering image retrieval, processing time, and video-generation efficiency.
  • Scientific limitations: Recognizing that image differences can also result from noise, calibration, exposure, or instrumental effects, and should not automatically be interpreted as confirmed astronomical discoveries.

Our vision is to turn the universe's hidden infrared observations into an interactive journey of discovery—helping everyone explore what lies BEYOND SPACE.
